players.product: Advantage2 annealing quantum computers and dual-rail superconducting gate-model systems (Quantum Circuits)

quarterly_data.signal: D-Wave Q2 2026 revenue was $3.1 million, essentially flat year-over-year, from approximately 100 customers; 62.4% of revenue came from commercial enterprises (Q2 2025: 45.1%) and Forbes Global 2000 customers accounted for 47.7% (Q2 2025: 20.4%). QCaaS subscription revenue was $1.9 million, up 50%; professional services approximately $900,000, up over 18%; systems and other approximately $300,000, mainly installation and site prep for the Florida Atlantic University system.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $3.1 million (flat); QCaaS $1.9 million (+50%); commercial 62.4%; Forbes Global 2000 47.7%

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 bookings were $2.1 million, up 59% from $1.3 million, with average booking size up over 87%; first-half 2026 bookings totaled $35.5 million, up 1,120% from $2.9 million, including a $20 million annealing quantum computer system for Florida Atlantic University. The dollar value of the sales opportunity pipeline rose over 120% from December 31, 2025 to June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 bookings $2.1 million (+59%); H1 bookings $35.5 million (+1,120%); pipeline up over 120%

quarterly_data.signal: Remaining performance obligations (backlog) totaled $40.7 million at June 30, 2026, up 668% from $5.3 million a year earlier; approximately 57% is expected to be recognized within the next 12 months and 72% within two years.
quarterly_data.figure: RPO $40.7 million (+668% from $5.3 million); ~57% within 12 months, 72% within two years

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 GAAP gross profit was $1.7 million and gross margin 55.4% (Q2 2025: 63.8%), lower on increased personnel costs; net loss was $48 million, or $0.13 per share; adjusted EBITDA loss was $37.1 million (Q2 2025: $20 million), up on product development and go-to-market investment. Cash and marketable investment securities were $546.2 million at June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin 55.4%; net loss $48 million; adjusted EBITDA loss $37.1 million; cash and marketable securities $546.2 million

quarterly_data.signal: First-half 2026 revenue was $5.9 million versus $18.1 million (H1 2025 included $13.7 million from the first annealing system sale); commercial customers were 67.7% of H1 revenue (16% in H1 2025) and Forbes Global 2000 customers 48.5% (7.5%). Over 37% ($1.3 million) of H1 QCaaS revenue came from business applications in production, versus 9.8% (approximately $300,000) a year earlier; H1 QCaaS revenue was $3.6 million, up over 30%, and professional services $1.9 million, up 22%.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 revenue $5.9 million; production applications over 37% ($1.3 million) of QCaaS revenue; H1 QCaaS $3.6 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO outlook: D-Wave still expects to ship two annealing quantum computer systems over the balance of the year, both likely in the fourth quarter, with some installation and calibration revenue carrying into 2027; it therefore expects third-quarter revenue to be up modestly from Q2 and fourth-quarter revenue up significantly over Q3, making up the majority of the year's revenue. CFO: D-Wave has the opportunity to be the first independent, publicly held quantum computing company to achieve sustained profitability.
quarterly_data.figure: two annealing systems to ship, likely in the fourth quarter; Q3 revenue up modestly; Q4 the majority of the year

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Florida Atlantic University: D-Wave expects to deliver the $20 million annealing system to Florida Atlantic University in 2026 and continues to expect to book two to three system deals annually, including two system deliveries in 2026. CFO: annealing system pricing ranges from $20 million to $40 million, the lower end for research labs and universities (the FAU price); revenue is recognized on average over about two quarters once the site is ready.
quarterly_data.figure: $20 million system; two to three system deals annually; system pricing $20 million to $40 million

quarterly_data.signal: Gate-model roadmap (CEO): a 17-physical-qubit dual-rail system later this year designed for logical error rates approximately 2x lower than physical (still on track before year-end); a 49-qubit system next year (approximately 20-fold error reduction); a 181-qubit system in 2028 (approximately 2,000-fold); a 10-logical-qubit system by 2030; and 100 logical qubits with more than 1 million reliable operations by 2032 for initial commercial applications such as quantum chemistry and quantum AI. The roadmap targets a Lambda of 10 (versus approximately two demonstrated by leading superconducting approaches), which could let approximately 100-200 physical qubits form one logical qubit.
quarterly_data.figure: 17 qubits later this year; 49 qubits next year; 181 qubits in 2028; 10 logical qubits by 2030; 100 logical qubits by 2032; Lambda 10 target

quarterly_data.signal: D-Wave published peer-reviewed research in Nature showing a two-qubit entangling gate with approximately 99.9% fidelity and gate times of about 500 nanoseconds on its eight-qubit dual-rail processor, enabled by native hardware-level error detection. CEO: the integration of Quantum Circuits (acquired in January) has gone extremely well, with technology shared between the annealing and gate-model programs.
quarterly_data.figure: ~99.9% two-qubit fidelity; ~500 nanoseconds; eight-qubit dual-rail processor

quarterly_data.signal: Annealing roadmap (Investor Day): scaling with advanced packaging and superconducting interconnects that link multiple QPUs in a multi-chip fabric, targeting a 20,000-qubit Advantage3 system in 2029 and 100,000 qubits by 2031; D-Wave also announced a scalable I/O prototype design to expand QPUs without a matching increase in control lines, and a gate-model simulator for error-aware programming expected in its Leap cloud later this year.

Customer AT&T: last week D-Wave announced an expanded agreement with AT&T to apply its technology to network-operations optimization, initially integrating annealing quantum computing with the agentic AI tools AT&T already uses; in one early application processing time fell from approximately one hour to less than 15 seconds, and AT&T plans to evaluate outage response, technician routing, and network planning and traffic management.
quarterly_data.figure: processing time from approximately one hour to less than 15 seconds

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Optum (a subsidiary of UnitedHealth Group): its initial proof of technology on D-Wave's quantum hybrid technology was strong enough to move directly to a production application, launched in May; Optum had run approximately 30,000 jobs by mid-June and is evaluating further opportunities within Optum and UnitedHealth. CEO: D-Wave now has six customer applications in production.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 30,000 jobs by mid-June; six customer applications in production

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: two government contracts are already in place and generating initial revenue on D-Wave's gate-model systems, and more than one company is interested in purchasing a dual-rail system.

CEO: the pipeline for both QCaaS and systems is expanding rapidly, with larger deals at larger companies (others closed in Q2 not yet announceable); maybe 25%-30% of commercial discussions are now with a line of business, versus none a year ago. CEO: only D-Wave's annealing systems deliver commercial production value today; gate-model systems will not be commercially relevant before 100 logical qubits around 2032.
quarterly_data.figure: maybe 25%-30% of discussions with a line of business

connects_to.relationship: D-Wave annealing quantum computing for mobile-network paging optimization (pilot; production deployment planned)

contracts.signal: CEO: NTT Docomo has expanded its production use of D-Wave technology - after a first application that cut paging signals across its Japanese mobile network by 15%, a second application reduced location registration signals by approximately 65% while reducing paging signals by 7% during peak periods; NTT Docomo said the results exceeded expectations and intends to identify further areas for D-Wave quantum optimization.
